blueprint.title: A Morning Errand in the City
blueprint.setting: Beijing, modern day, morning to early afternoon
blueprint.problem: 李明 needs to pay a utility bill before the bank closes
blueprint.incitingEvent: 李明 arrives at the bank and sees a notice about an unexpected closure

beats.what: He gets ready, grabs his wallet and heads out to the bank
beats.because: the story opens with 李明 needing to pay the bill

beats.what: He discovers a sign: “因电力故障，银行提前关闭，今天的业务已发生”
beats.because: because the bank is closed, he must find another way to pay
beats.arrivedHow: walks down the street from his apartment

beats.what: He meets 小红, who tells him she is 来自加拿大, a different 国家, and suggests using the post office’s payment service
beats.because: because 小红 offers an alternative place to settle the bill
beats.arrivedHow: takes the next block east to the post office

beats.where: Internet café on the second floor of the post office building
beats.what: They log in, chat about their daily 生活, and complete the online payment
beats.because: because the post office requires online payment, they go to the café
beats.arrivedHow: takes the elevator up to the café

beats.what: The transaction is successful, the café announces it will 结束 soon, and 李明 leaves relieved
beats.because: because the payment is finally done, the story’s problem ends

blueprint.resolution: 李明 pays the bill successfully and can continue his day without worry

targetPlan.why: The sign at the bank explains that a power outage has occurred, so the word '发生' naturally appears.
小红 mentions the country she is from, making '国家' necessary in the dialogue.
小红 says she '来自' Canada, requiring the verb.
While waiting, they talk about their daily life, so '生活' fits naturally.
The café announces it will close soon, using the word '结束' to indicate termination.

blueprints.label: B

blueprint.title: The Lost Passenger
blueprint.setting: A busy Tuesday afternoon in the city center, near a subway station and a park.
blueprint.problem: Little Ming has lost his new pen, which was a gift from a friend from another country.
blueprint.incitingEvent: Little Ming realizes the pen is missing during math class, causing panic before he can leave for the day.

beats.what: Little Ming is crying because he cannot find his special pen. Li Ming asks what happened.
beats.because: the story opens

beats.where: A small coffee shop near the school
beats.what: Li Ming listens to Little Ming's story. Little Ming explains he bought the pen at a gift shop. He describes it as a gift from a friend from another country.
beats.because: Li Ming needs details to help search
beats.arrivedHow: Walking from the school gate to the nearby cafe (5 mins)

beats.where: The suburban park where they did homework yesterday
beats.what: They search the park. It is quiet. Li Ming suggests looking in the usual spot. They spot Xiaohong sitting on a bench, looking at a pen.
beats.because: The last known location of the pen is the park
beats.arrivedHow: Taking a shared bike from the cafe to the park (10 mins)

beats.what: Li Ming approaches Xiaohong. Little Ming recognizes the pen. Xiaohong says she found it on the grass yesterday and kept it for its owner.
beats.because: They saw a familiar object with a stranger

beats.what: Xiaohong returns the pen. Little Ming is very happy. They talk about how they lost and found it. Li Ming says this is a good end to the busy day.
beats.because: The owner and finder have met

blueprint.resolution: The pen is returned to Little Ming, resolving the loss and the emotional distress.

targetPlan.why: Li Ming asks 'What happened?'. This is the most natural, high-frequency usage for 发生 when asking about an immediate, visible negative event.
Little Ming needs to describe the origin of the pen to help Li Ming identify it if they find it. He says 'It comes from a friend...'
Continuing the description, Little Ming specifies the friend is 'from another country'. This requires the noun 国家.
Xiaohong explains she didn't know who it belonged to, so she kept it to see if the owner or someone else (other people) would come looking for it.
After the resolution, Li Ming comments that the 'day' or the 'incident' has finished/ended. He might say 'Today's trouble is finished.'
In a concluding reflection, Li Ming might make a simple philosophical point suitable for HSK 3, such as 'Life is full of small surprises' or 'This is part of daily life.'
Little Ming thanks Xiaohong. She replies, 'Of course (当然), I would help you.' This fits the polite, positive resolution.
During the conversation after returning the pen, Little Ming might suggest, 'You can come to our house to play, or (或者) we can go buy ice cream.'

blueprint.title: The International Street Festival
blueprint.setting: A rainy Saturday afternoon in a busy city district with international shops and food stalls.
blueprint.problem: Li Ming and Xiaohong want to find a specific European grocery store to buy ingredients for dinner, but the sign is missing and they only have a vague, possibly incorrect, description.
blueprint.incitingEvent: Li Ming receives a text with a picture of a store front but the store name is blurry, only showing it is for a specific country's food.

beats.what: Li Ming shows Xiaohong a blurry photo on his phone. He says he wants to buy food. Xiaohong asks where. Li Ming guesses the store is for a foreign country.
beats.because: the story opens

beats.what: They rush to the subway. Xiaohong asks what country the store is from. Li Ming says it is difficult to know. He thinks maybe France, or maybe Italy.
beats.because: they need to travel to the city center to find the area mentioned in the photo

beats.what: They arrive and look for the store. The street is crowded due to a small festival. They see many signs but none match. Li Ming is worried the event will last too long.
beats.because: they took the subway to the location of the store

beats.what: Xiaohong finds a person selling flags. She asks where the French or Italian store is. The seller points to the end of the street. They start walking there.
beats.because: they realized they couldn't find it by looking at distant signs in the crowd

beats.where: The end of the street, in front of a shop
beats.what: They find a shop with no sign, only a French flag. Li Ming checks his photo. It matches. He realizes what happened with the blurry name.
beats.because: they followed the direction given by the seller

beats.what: The bell rings as they enter. The store is small but has what they need. They buy the items and prepare to leave as the festival starts to wind down.
beats.because: they confirmed this was the right store

blueprint.resolution: They successfully identify and enter the correct store by recognizing the national flag, resolving the confusion caused by the blurry photo.

targetPlan.why: Xiaohong tries to narrow down the search by asking the origin of the food store, e.g., 'This store comes from which country?'
Used in the question about the specific nation, e.g., 'Which country does it come from?' to define the search parameter.
Li Ming expresses uncertainty between two options, e.g., 'Maybe France, or (或者) maybe Italy?'
Li Ming considers if it might be any other place if not the first two guesses, e.g., 'Or perhaps some other (其他) place?'
Xiaohong responds to Li Ming's worry about the crowd, saying of course they will find it, or Li Ming says of course he is worried, establishing their attitude.
Li Ming reflects on the situation, realizing what happened (what occurred) to make the sign unreadable or why he didn't recognize it immediately.
They notice the festival is finishing or their errand is finishing, providing a natural closing thought to the scene.

blueprint.title: A Morning Errand in the City
blueprint.setting: Beijing, modern day, early morning to late afternoon
blueprint.problem: 妈妈的感冒药忘在家里，李明必须赶快去药店买药，否则她会不舒服。
blueprint.incitingEvent: 李明早上起床发现妈妈的药不在药箱里。

beats.what: 李明检查药箱，发现药不见了，决定立刻去最近的药店。
beats.because: 故事开端，李明发现问题需要解决。

beats.what: 李明走出小区，穿过马路到药店。
beats.because: 因为药不在家里，他必须去药店买药。

beats.what: 刚进门就发生停电，店内灯光全部熄灭，顾客只能等。
beats.because: 因为他已经到达药店，才会遇到突发的停电。

beats.what: 在等待恢复电力时，李明看到一张宣传单，上面写着“来自法国的文化展”，提到不同国家的艺术。
beats.because: 因为停电让他有时间站在柜台旁，看到宣传单。

beats.what: 电力恢复后，李明买到药，回到家把药交给妈妈，事情结束，感叹今天的生活充满意外。
beats.because: 因为停电结束后他才能完成购买，回家解决了最初的问题。

blueprint.resolution: 妈妈得到感冒药，身体好转，李明体会到即使是普通的生活也会有意外的发现。

targetPlan.why: 停电是一个突发事件，必须用‘发生’来描述这种意外。
宣传单介绍的是来自法国的文化展，需要提到‘国家’来说明来源。
在药买完并交给妈妈后，整个紧急的事情‘结束’了。
宣传单上写着‘来自法国的文化展’，需要用‘来自’说明展览的来源。
李明在回顾今天的经历时，用‘生活’来概括日常中的小插曲。

draft.title: 丢失的钢笔
draft.content:
星期二下午三点，小明站在学校门口哭。
他找不到他的新钢笔，心里非常着急。
李明看见他，走过去问发生了什么事。
小明说：“我的钢笔不见了，我非常生气。”
李明安慰他，让他不要着急，一起找找。
他们来到附近的小咖啡店坐下休息。
小明说：“这支笔是我的外国朋友送的礼物。”
李明问：“那个朋友来自哪个国家？”
小明回答：“他来自另一个国家，笔很特别。”
李明说：“知道了，我们回公园找找吧。”
他们骑共享单车去了昨天的公园。
公园里很安静，只有几个人在散步。
李明说：“你昨天在哪里做作业？”
小明说：“就在那个长椅旁边。”
他们开始在草地上仔细寻找。
突然，他们看见小红坐在长椅上。
她手里拿着一支蓝色的钢笔。
李明走过去，问小红那是不是她的笔。
小明跑过去，一眼就认出了自己的笔。
小红说：“是我昨天在草地上捡到的。
我不认识你，也没看到其他主人。
所以我把笔留着，等人来拿。”
小红把钢笔还给了小明。
小明笑了，不再担心，事情结束了。
李明说：“这是今天忙碌生活的结束。”
小明对小红说：“谢谢你，你当然会帮我。”
小红说：“当然，我们是好朋友。
或者我们一起去吃冰淇淋庆祝一下？”

preRepairCritique.strengths: The basic structure of a lost-and-found story is present, providing a clear framework for entry-level learners.
preRepairCritique.weaknesses: The integration of target vocabulary is extremely forced and unnatural (e.g., "这是今天忙碌生活的结束" is not something natives say in this context; "你当然会帮我" is a weird thing to say to a new friend).
